reason: Half one is real and driven; half two is fabricated and its half of the fix would make the artifact worse. VERIFIED (guest half): b.css:365 `.b-item:hover .b-copy, .b-item:focus-within .b-copy` is unscoped - no @media (hover), no owner scope - and `.b-grab` is emitted only when `owner` is true (render-b.js:159). Driving phone and desk at 390 and 1440, rows whose `.b-item` contains no `.b-grab` and whose computed cursor is `auto` go from `rgba(0,0,0,0)` / `none` to `rgba(255,255,255,0.04)` with `rgba(255,255,255,0.04) 0 0 0 12px` on hover. It is not inherited from an owner-only rule; it renders on the guest surfaces themselves. Worse, and unnamed by the finding: b.css:688 `.b-item:active .b-copy { background: var(--fore-10) }` is unscoped too, so on the phone - the audience's actual device, where hover never fires - pressing a guest row paints it at `rgba(255,255,255,0.1)`, the exact ink density the file reserves for pressing a real control, and `document.body.innerHTML` is byte-identical before and after; nothing opens, nothing navigates. The file's own comments state the model this contradicts: `.b-behindSummary` is commented 'the only control a guest is given', and the behaviour gate at interaction-check.mjs:2172 opens with 'A guest row carries no control'. Seven rows answer a press like a button and the product means none of them. The gate asserts nothing about this; it only asserts guest titles are never trimmed. REFUTED (crowded-owner half): there is no crowded owner row in the artifact at either viewport the finding claims to have driven. Sweeping owner-flight, owner-editing, owner-undone and publish across 360/390/414/600/701/768/900/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440/1920, `data-crowded="true"` never appears on a row carrying a `.b-grab` at 390 or 1440 - it appears on exactly one owner row at 360px, below the graded floor and outside the resize set. The only crowded rows that exist anywhere are five GUEST rows in the day state's 'behind you' past rail, all `grab:false`, measured at `rgb(17,17,17)` plate and ring, unchanged on hover. So the specificity tie at b.css:371 is true as CSS and inert as behaviour: it suppresses a hover answer only on rows that carry no control - which is precisely what half one argues should happen. The finding's driven claim about it is not something that could have been observed. And the fix for it would be a regression: reordering the crowded rule under a `--row-fill` custom property and asserting that a crowded row's background changes under hover would restore a hover answer to those five non-control guest rows, and would swap the opaque #111 plate - the thing that keeps stacked crowded titles legible where they cross the rail and its leader - for a 4% translucent tint the rail bleeds through. Confirmed on the guest half only, with the fix stripped to it.
sharpenedFix: Keep only the first line of the proposed fix, and extend it to the press state the finding missed - the one that matters on a phone. In b.css scope all three row-level answers to rows that can actually be opened: line 365 becomes `.b-item:has(.b-grab):hover .b-copy, .b-item:has(.b-grab):focus-within .b-copy`, and line 688's `.b-item:active .b-copy` becomes `.b-item:has(.b-grab):active .b-copy`. (`:focus-within` is already dead on a guest row - nothing inside `.b-copy` is focusable there - so `:hover` and `:active` are the whole defect.) DISCARD the second half entirely: do not reorder `.b-item[data-crowded="true"] .b-copy`, do not route the plate through `--row-fill`, and do not add the proposed assertion that a crowded row's background changes under hover - every crowded row in the artifact is a guest row, and that change would reintroduce the same affordance lie on the past rail while thinning the opaque plate to a translucent tint. While in that declaration, close the seam it exposes: `:active` sets `background: var(--fore-10)` but leaves the 12px ring at `var(--fore-04)`, so a pressed owner row today renders a 10% plate inside a 4% halo. Give the active rule its matching `box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px var(--fore-10)`. Then assert the inverse of what the finding proposed: on phone, desk, day and print at 390, a `.b-item` with no `.b-grab` must report identical computed `background-color` and `box-shadow` at rest, under hover, and under a held pointer.
